CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Answer the U.S. List 4 announcement and currency-manipulator designation with a calibrated, reversible package: keep the halt on new U.S. farm purchases, prepare a proportional tariff response on remaining U.S. goods timed to 1 September if List 4 takes effect, and leave the September Washington talks slot open. Do not offer purchase or structural concessions while new U.S. tariffs are pending, and do not yet fire reserve cards (rare-earth export curbs or a broad unreliable-entity crackdown). The aim is to restore deterrence after the Osaka truce was broken without exhausting limited ammunition or accelerating capital-flight risk.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is high, not existential. Combined U.S. Section 301 coverage is already ~$250B at 25%; on 1 August Trump added 10% on the remaining ~$300B effective 1 September, covering nearly all leftover consumer/electronics exports after Shanghai talks produced little progress and after the 29 June Osaka pledge of no new tariffs “for the time being.” Huawei remains on the Entity List with Google/chip-supplier cutoffs, which hits a national-champion and tech-autonomy goal. After CNY broke 7, Treasury labeled China a currency manipulator (first since 1994)—mostly symbolic near-term but a financial-and-reputational escalation. Macro already shows the bite: China industrial production YoY slowed from 108.5 (Mar) to 104.4 (Aug); SA merchandise exports fell ~5.6% over the window; CNY weakened from ~6.71 to ~7.06. Reserves are still ~$3.13T and IP is still expanding, so this is the +0.5 CHN anchor (export-sector hit, FX pressure, Huawei targeting), not +1.0. Action should be retaliate rather than maximal escalate or concede: China has already said it will take “necessary countermeasures” and has halted U.S. ag purchases; caving now would invite another hike (Trump has already floated lifting List 4 “well beyond 25%”). Full non-tariff escalation (rare earths, broad unreliable-list implementation) would also hurt Chinese suppliers and risk a faster yuan/reserve drain. The U.S. is feeling pain too (Michigan sentiment 98.4→89.8, 10-year yield 2.65%→1.71%, VIX spike to 24.6 on 5 August, Fed funds cut to 2.13%), so a proportional farm/tariff response can raise U.S. political cost without closing the pre-1 September talk window.
key_factors: List 4: 10% on remaining ~$300B Chinese goods from 1 Sept, breaking the Osaka no-new-tariffs truce
Huawei Entity List plus Android/chip-supplier cutoff still in force
Treasury currency-manipulator designation after CNY broke 7 (first since 1994)
China IP YoY 108.5→104.4 and SA exports down ~5.6%; yuan ~6.71→7.06; reserves still ~$3.13T
China already halted U.S. farm purchases and publicly pledged countermeasures; remaining U.S.-goods tariff ammunition is limited
U.S. side also weakening (sentiment crash, 10-year collapse, VIX spike, rate cut), which preserves some leverage if retaliation stays calibrated

sources_cited.excerpt: After the Shanghai round, Trump announces 10% tariffs on the remaining ~$300B of Chinese goods (List 4), effective Sept 1.
After CNY breaks 7 per USD, US Treasury designates China a currency manipulator (first such designation since 1994).
G20 Osaka: Trump and Xi agree to resume talks. Existing tariffs remain; no new tariffs "for the time being."
US Commerce Department adds Huawei and affiliates to the Entity List. US firms generally barred from selling to Huawei without a license.
Google suspends Huawei's access to Android updates / GMS; major US chip suppliers pause sales.
China industrial production YoY index latest 104.4 (2019-08-01), down from 108.5 in March.
China SA merchandise exports latest $206.6B (2019-08-01), down ~5.6% from $219.0B in March.
CNY/USD monthly average 7.0629 in August 2019 vs 6.7119 in March (~5.2% depreciation).
U.S. Michigan consumer sentiment dropped to 89.8 in August from 98.4 in July.
U.S. 10-year yield 1.71% on 2019-08-07, down from 2.65% in mid-February.
China vowed to take "necessary countermeasures"; ambassador: if the U.S. wishes to talk we will talk, if they want to fight we will fight.
China Commerce Ministry: related companies have suspended purchases of U.S. agricultural products; will not rule out tariffs on farm goods bought after Aug. 3.
Treasury determined China is a Currency Manipulator and will engage the IMF; cited CNY devaluation after List 4 announcement.
